newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Gov't in no hurry to sell Nordbanken stake.
newsitem.headline: Gov't in no hurry to sell Nordbanken stake.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday the government was in no hurry to sell its 59.4 percent stake in bank Nordbanken.
"We are not bound by any timetable," Asbrink said at a news conference after visiting some companies in southern Sweden. "We are not relying on getting that money now."

Sweden's National Debt Office in its budget forecast last week said it saw a deficit of 12 billion crowns this year when including an expected 26 billion crown income from the sale of Nordbanken shares.
"The National Debt Office has to stand for that assessment," he said. "It's the office's estimates."
Asbrink refrained from saying if a sale would take place this year.
He said, however, that it would be desireable for Nordbanken to take part in the current banking sector restructuring but did not want to target possible scenarios.
"I don't want to speculate on exactly to whom (we will sell) and when it will happen," he said.
"We want to be well paid," Asbrink said, but added the government also has a responsibility to contribute to strong structural solutions and a responsibility for staff.
